harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created an encrypted volume on node1 (AlmaLinux 9) using a 1GB file-backed LUKS2 container (/var/lib/secure-volume/secure.img) unlocked via a root-only keyfile (/etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/srv-secure.key), mapped to /dev/mapper/secure_srv and formatted ext4, mounted at /srv/secure. Configured /etc/crypttab (noauto luks entry) and /etc/fstab (with x-systemd.requires= on the cryptsetup service) so systemd's generated mount unit automatically pulls in decryption and mounts /srv/secure at every boot without any interactive input. Verified end-to-end: rebooted node1 via `systemctl reboot`, confirmed boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and confirmed /srv/secure was auto-mounted post-boot with the pre-restart test file's SHA-256 checksum unchanged.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/disk layout (AlmaLinux 9.6, single vda disk, no spare block device)
Installed cryptsetup package
Created 1G backing file /var/lib/secure-volume/secure.img and 4096-byte random keyfile /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/srv-secure.key (mode 600)
Ran cryptsetup luksFormat (LUKS2) on the backing file using the keyfile
Opened the LUKS container as /dev/mapper/secure_srv, formatted ext4, mounted at /srv/secure
Added crypttab entry (secure_srv luks,noauto) and fstab entry (with x-systemd.requires=systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service) for auto-unlock and auto-mount at boot
Verified the systemd-generated srv-secure.mount unit correctly pulls in the cryptsetup service when started, confirming boot-time dependency wiring
Wrote a healthcheck test file with a captured SHA-256 checksum, and captured pre-restart boot_id baseline
Triggered systemctl reboot on node1, polled until exec access returned
Confirmed new boot_id (proving actual restart) and verified /srv/secure was automatically unlocked and mounted with no manual steps, with the healthcheck file's checksum unchanged

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline: encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure with data present pre-restart, and boot identity captured
evidence.summary: /srv/secure mounted from /dev/mapper/secure_srv (LUKS-backed), healthcheck.txt written with known SHA-256, pre-restart boot_id=31b01b46-96de-4ded-a021-49887e7d4053 captured

evidence.requirement: Auto-unlock/auto-mount configuration in place (crypttab + fstab with systemd dependency) validated before reboot
evidence.summary: crypttab (noauto luks entry) and fstab (x-systemd.requires=systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service) entries added; manually starting srv-secure.mount unit correctly triggered the cryptsetup dependency and mounted the volume, proving the wiring works
systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded/delayed subshell so the exec call returned REBOOT_TRIGGERED before the node went down

evidence.requirement: Node restart confirmed unreachable then reachable again, with changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Immediately after reboot trigger, exec timed out (node down); subsequent poll succeeded with new boot_id=b22cc786-326c-4cfa-826e-133f121ad6ec (differs from baseline) and new uptime-since timestamp

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: encrypted volume auto-unlocked, mounted, and data intact without manual intervention
evidence.summary: Post-boot, systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service and srv-secure.mount both show Active since the boot time (auto-started, no manual commands run), /srv/secure is mounted from /dev/mapper/secure_srv, and healthcheck.txt SHA-256 matches the pre-restart baseline exactly
